cases.question: Where does Maestro keep a Claude Code session's ephemeral state on disk, which files are in it, and how does a hook or CLI script work out which session it belongs to? What happens when it cannot tell?
cases.expected: One directory per session: <project>/.claude/maestro_sessions/<session_id>/ holding log.jsonl (append-only session log), session.json ({workflow, generated_instances, run_id}, plus meeting/worktree/session-name keys) and tasks.json (success-path steps that already have a TaskCreate); maestro_sessions/ gets a .gitignore containing `*`. apps/maestro/src/core/session-paths.ts owns the question: resolveSessionId takes payload.session_id when the caller is a hook with a stdin payload, else the CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID env var (the !-injected gate scripts and CLIs with no stdin), else null. The id is validated against ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,128}$, never sanitised, and an invalid id from either source is null without falling through to the other. With no session the caller writes nothing and exits 0, which looks like Maestro not being installed. A subagent's hook payload carries the main session's session_id, so one workflow run is one directory.
cases.skill_note: maestro-architecture (root, listed at init): its description already names the directory, the three files and the resolution order (payload session_id -> CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID -> null); its session-state sub-concept names session-paths.ts, the validation rule and the silent exit-0 degradation. The model can answer from the skill and open one file to confirm instead of searching for where session files are written.
